app.name: Warrior Identity Academy
app.tagline: Become who you decided to be.

noWarrior.title: No warrior chosen
noWarrior.body: The workshop belongs to one warrior at a time. Choose who is doing the work.

commitment.line1: A great life begins when a person takes a stand on who he wants to become.
commitment.line2: First, radical identity change. Then, radical behavior change.
commitment.line3: Decide, with immense seriousness, who you want to become. This commitment becomes the standard that judges everything you do next.
commitment.epigraph: "This commitment will become your personal religion — the standard that judges your behavior."
commitment.statementLabel: The kind of person I want to become

idealSelves.intro: You're not one person — you're a constellation. Name two or three ideal selves that deeply inspire you.
idealSelves.guardrail: Not fantasies of status, pleasure or wealth — visions of the kind of person you want to be.
idealSelves.epigraph: "Your personal myth is that story. And you're the only one who can write it."
idealSelves.taglinePlaceholder: I read seriously and think carefully.
idealSelves.descriptionHint: Two or three sentences. Present tense. "I am…", not "I want to become…".
idealSelves.wantWarning: Present tense: write "I am…", not "I want to…".
idealSelves.inspiration: Sides of you — tap to start a self
idealSelves.countHint: Two to three selves. Each needs a name and a description.
idealSelves.needActive: Mark one self as active — it sets your theme.

futureBiography.chooseLabel: Which of your ideal selves calls to you most? Pick one — provisionally is fine.
futureBiography.write: Write the Wikipedia entry of your most beloved ideal self. Describe your achievements and interests as if they were already fact.
futureBiography.epigraph: "Now write your own. Don't be modest."
futureBiography.articleHint: Third person, encyclopedic, stated as fact.
futureBiography.exampleText: Omar F. Najjarine is an American polymath, lecturer and essayist. His work spans philosophy, psychology, literature and cultural criticism, unified by a central concern for the first principles and noble ends of a well-lived life. His most celebrated work, the three-volume What Should a Human Being Grow Towards?, has been described as a "university without walls."
futureBiography.horizonHint: Optional. The year this entry is read.

attractions.intro: Your purpose has probably been speaking to you for years — through fascinations, recurring interests, the projects you lose yourself in.
attractions.epigraph: "Where has life already been calling me?"
attractions.receptiveHelp: Three to five moments when something you encountered deeply moved, inspired or fascinated you.
attractions.receptivePlaceholder: An essay, a hero, a place, a film scene…
attractions.participatoryHelp: Three to five moments you felt alive because of what you were doing — moments you loved participating in reality.
attractions.participatoryPlaceholder: A project, a conversation, a thing you made…
attractions.insightPlaceholder: Optional. What do the two lists have in common?

emergencyKit.intro: Build your "Break in Case of Emergency" kit: anything that restores you to your higher self when you're demoralized, lonely, hopeless, cynical or lost.
emergencyKit.use: When demoralization or lethargy strikes, open this kit and let it remind you who you are and what you're here to do.
emergencyKit.titlePlaceholder: The poems of T.S. Eliot read by Jeremy Irons
emergencyKit.empty: The kit is empty. Add at least one item.
emergencyKit.example1: The poems of T.S. Eliot read by Jeremy Irons

lifeRules.intro: Your life gives you feedback every day. Write down what poisons you and what strengthens you — your own commandments.
lifeRules.epigraph: "The undocumented life is not worth examining." — William Vallicella
lifeRules.avoidHelp: List the things that reliably make you worse.
lifeRules.haveHelp: List the things that reliably make you better.
lifeRules.pacing: Don't rush this. Think from experience. Think from regret.
lifeRules.closing: It doesn't mean you'll always obey your list. But failing is much better than being lost.

firstPractice.directive: Meditate for at least 10 minutes a day.
firstPractice.rule1: Sit in complete silence for at least 10 minutes.
firstPractice.why: You're training dis-identification: you're not the weather your mind produces, you're the sky it appears in.
firstPractice.defaultDescription: Sit in complete silence for at least 10 minutes. Remain awake. Return tomorrow.
firstPractice.anchorHint: Accepting adds this as a daily anchor on your dashboard.

done.title: This is who we are now
done.body: The identity work is on record. Now the nervous system learns — by simple, unfanciful repetition.
done.again: Your practice is waiting on the dashboard.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.mvwHint: Reduce to the essentials. Your streak and XP are safe.
dashboard.focusHint: One domain grows at ×{mult} this quarter. Every other domain is in Maintenance Mode. Tap again to clear.
dashboard.focusNone: No focus chosen. All domains in Maintenance Mode.
dashboard.mvwPick: Which anchors will you keep? (at least one)

journal.title: Journal
journal.placeholder: What happened today? What did you notice?
journal.empty: No entries yet. Write your first line.
journal.replayHint: Swipe through your last seven days
journal.tagPlaceholder: Add a tag and press Enter
journal.confirmDelete: Delete this entry? The XP you earned stays with you.
journal.noWarrior: Choose a warrior before you open the journal.

reflections.title: Reflections
reflections.historyEmpty: No past reflections yet. The first one is the hardest.
reflections.gateHint: Gates open near the end of each period, or when the last one was missed.
reflections.noWarrior: Choose a warrior before you reflect.
reflections.emptyAnswer: Write at least one answer before saving.

weekly.w1: What reliably made me stronger this week?
weekly.w2: What poisoned me? Which life rule did I break, and under what conditions?
weekly.w3: Did I sit in silence each day? What did the sky notice about the weather?
weekly.w4: What would my ideal self do differently next week?

monthly.m1: Which of my must-haves did I actually honor this month?
monthly.m2: Which must-avoid crept back in? What let it in?
monthly.m3: What new fact could my Wikipedia entry state after this month?
monthly.m4: Which pattern showed up often enough to become a new life rule?

quarterly.q1: Read your ideal selves again. Which one is winning, and what proves it?
quarterly.q2: What hard-won lesson from this quarter deserves to become a law?
quarterly.q3: What pulled me most — what did I love to take in, and to do?
quarterly.q4: What is the one behaviour change for the coming quarter?

ai.empty: Nothing to work with yet — write something first.
ai.externalHelper: Copy the prompt into any outside model, then paste its reply here. The result is stored beside your original — the original is never overwritten.
ai.promptFallback: Clipboard unavailable — copy the prompt manually:
ai.parseError: Could not read that reply. It should contain a `refined:` or `translated(en|he):` line.
ai.noPatterns: No patterns yet. Write a few entries, then look again.
ai.noEntries: No journal entries to read yet.
ai.nothingFound: Nothing stood out this time. Keep writing.
